findings.title: CloudTrail logging should be enabled
findings.description: Without CloudTrail, API activity is not recorded, leaving no audit trail for detection or incident response.
findings.remediation: Create a trail and start logging via `aws cloudtrail start-logging`.
findings.evidence: No CloudTrail trail is configured in this account/region.

findings.title: CloudTrail should be multi-region
findings.description: A multi-region trail captures activity in every region, including ones an attacker might use precisely because they are unmonitored.
findings.remediation: Enable IsMultiRegionTrail on the trail.

findings.title: CloudTrail log file validation should be enabled
findings.description: Log file validation produces a tamper-evident digest so you can prove logs were not altered or deleted after the fact.
findings.remediation: Enable log file validation on the trail (EnableLogFileValidation).

findings.title: CloudTrail logs should be encrypted with a KMS key
findings.description: Encrypting trail logs with a customer-managed KMS key protects their confidentiality and adds an access-control boundary around them.
findings.remediation: Set a KmsKeyId on the trail to enable SSE-KMS on delivered logs.

findings.title: Security groups should not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22 (SSH)
findings.description: SSH open to the entire internet exposes hosts to credential brute-force and exploitation of the SSH service.
findings.remediation: Restrict port 22 to known admin CIDRs or a bastion/SSM Session Manager; never use 0.0.0.0/0.

findings.title: Security groups should not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to all ports
findings.description: An 'all traffic' rule from anywhere removes the network boundary entirely, exposing every listening service on attached instances.
findings.remediation: Replace the all-ports/all-protocols rule with least-privilege rules.

findings.title: IAM password policy should require a minimum length of 14
findings.description: A strong account password policy resists brute-force and guessing attacks against console users.
findings.remediation: Set a password policy with MinimumPasswordLength >= 14 via `aws iam update-account-password-policy`.

findings.title: IAM users with console access should have MFA enabled
findings.description: MFA adds a second factor so a leaked password alone cannot grant console access.
findings.remediation: Enable an MFA device for every user that has a login profile.
findings.evidence: User has console access but no MFA device registered.

findings.title: IAM users should not have AdministratorAccess attached directly
findings.description: Attaching AdministratorAccess directly to users violates least privilege and makes a single credential compromise catastrophic. Grant broad permissions through assumable roles instead.
findings.remediation: Detach AdministratorAccess from the user and grant scoped permissions, using IAM roles for privileged operations.
findings.evidence: AdministratorAccess managed policy is attached directly to this user.

findings.title: IAM users should not have more than one active access key
findings.description: Multiple active access keys widen the attack surface and complicate rotation and revocation.
findings.remediation: Deactivate and delete unused access keys; keep at most one active key.

findings.title: S3 buckets should block all public access
findings.description: S3 Block Public Access is a safety net that overrides bucket ACLs and policies that would otherwise expose data. All four settings should be on.
findings.remediation: Enable Block Public Access (BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets) at the bucket or, preferably, the account level via the S3 console or `aws s3api put-public-access-block`.

findings.remediation: Enable Block Public Access (BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets) at the bucket or, preferably, the account level via the S3 console or `aws s3api put-public-access-block`.

findings.title: S3 buckets should enable server-side encryption at rest
findings.description: Default encryption ensures every object written to the bucket is encrypted at rest without relying on clients to request it.
findings.remediation: Enable default encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS) on the bucket via `aws s3api put-bucket-encryption`.

findings.title: S3 bucket ACLs should not grant access to Everyone/AuthenticatedUsers
findings.description: ACL grants to the AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers groups expose bucket contents to anyone on the internet or any AWS account.
findings.remediation: Remove public ACL grants and prefer bucket policies with explicit principals; enable Block Public Access as a backstop.

findings.title: S3 bucket policies should not allow anonymous (Principal '*') access
findings.description: A bucket policy that Allows a wildcard principal without a restricting condition makes the bucket readable or writable by anyone.
findings.remediation: Scope bucket policy statements to specific principals, or add a restricting Condition (e.g. aws:SourceVpce) and enable Block Public Access.
findings.evidence: Bucket policy Allows a wildcard principal with no restricting Condition.

findings.title: S3 buckets should have versioning enabled
findings.description: Versioning preserves prior object versions, aiding recovery from accidental deletion and ransomware that overwrites objects.
findings.remediation: Enable versioning via `aws s3api put-bucket-versioning`.

findings.title: S3 buckets should have server access logging enabled
findings.description: Access logs record requests made to the bucket, supporting incident investigation and detection of unauthorized access.
findings.remediation: Configure access logging to a dedicated log bucket.
